evidence: Source review of the frozen bytes. Types: gates/render 1 criterion and gates/constraints 2 criteria, all type = "binary"; scored/functional 42 criteria, all type = "binary" (grep count 42, no points key); scored/polish 6 criteria, all binary; scored/visual 3 criteria, all type = "likert" with points = 5. Every binary criterion I read states an observable pass/fail behaviour with an explicit 'Fails if ...' clause (e.g. polish cw_narrow_width_usable: 'Fails if the page needs sideways scrolling, if any of those five areas cannot be reached ...'; cw_controls_feedback_and_labels: 'Fails if a main control has no readable name, or if any of the three actions ends with no visible textual feedback'). The colouring criteria that sound closest to craft are phrased as countable facts ('must show five visibly different treatments'), not degree. No craft or degree-of-quality judgement is typed binary: the three craft items (cw_visual_editor_readability, cw_visual_workspace_layout, cw_visual_component_finish) are likert, and each carries a described anchor at every level 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 and 0 (e.g. '5: clear grouping, consistent spacing, nothing overlapping or clipped. 4: one or two small spacing issues. 3: several crowded or uneven areas. 2: frequent overlap or clipping. 1: severe layout problems throughout. 0: no workspace is shown.'). This mirrors the frozen template's visual format. visual/prompt.md is consistent with the anchors: 'Each criterion is scored from 0 to 5 using the anchors written in it ... 0 is used only when the thing being judged is not shown at all.' Per the skill's known false positive, the internal workbook note that likert is not used is not a finding. Notes (not defects of this row, both bounded): (a) cw_visual_editor_readability folds 'visibility of the caret and of a selection' into the scale, but only anchor 5 mentions them ('caret and selection easy to see'); levels 4 to 1 do not say where an otherwise clean editor with an invisible caret or selection lands, so a judge could give 4 ('one or two minor distractions') or 2. (b) In the hosted run on an EARLIER candidate the harness recorded raw 4 as value 0.75 and raw 5 as 1.0, i.e. (raw-1)/4, so anchors 1 and 0 appear to be worth the same; this is shared template/harness behaviour, not task-authored. Risk stays true because no configured judge run exists for these bytes: the visual likert ratings are unmeasured here (raw-evidence-index limitation: 'Visual ratings are not measured by a judge for these bytes'), and the scripted golden results do not exercise likert scoring.
suggested_fix: Optional: in cw_visual_editor_readability add caret/selection to a lower anchor, e.g. '3: usable but several readability flaws, or the caret or the selection is hard to see.'
